html:
The Ohlone, once called Costanoans from the Spanish for "coast people", are a Native American people of the California coast from San Francisco Bay to Monterey Bay and the lower Salinas Valley.

Before the Spanish came they lived in some fifty small, independent groups, each with a village or two, and spoke several related languages. Acorns, shellfish, fish and game fed them, and they left large shell mounds around the bay.

Spain arrived in 1769. Junípero Serra and other Franciscans founded seven missions in Ohlone land, including San Carlos at Carmel and San Francisco de Asís. Disease, forced labour and the break-up of family life killed most of the people within a few decades. Under Mexican and then American rule they lost their remaining land. Today several Ohlone groups, such as the Rumsen, are working to revive their languages. See also Ohlone on the modern map.
sum: The Ohlone, once called Costanoans from the Spanish for "coast people", are a Native American people of the California coast from San Francisco Bay to Monterey Bay and the lower Salinas Valley.
